**Observations from the test image:**
- Ground-level view of soybean plants with pronounced yellowing/chlorosis
- Visible leaves show interveinal chlorosis — yellow areas between veins while veins appear to remain greener
- Plants show general decline with dried/dead material mixed in
- Late-season appearance with patchy plant death

**Reasoning:**
The interveinal chlorosis pattern (yellow blotches between veins, green veins remaining) is the hallmark of **Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS)**. The SDS reference images confirm this pattern: large chlorotic and necrotic blotches between leaf veins while the midvein and lateral veins stay green. The late-season plant decline visible at ground level is also consistent with SDS field presentation. Brown Stem Rot can mimic this foliar pattern but would require internal stem browning to confirm — the overall presentation here aligns best with SDS.
